September 2026 — the forward plan PLAN

Frozen 31 Aug. A FORWARD PLAN, not a backtest. September has not happened. Only the 1-Sept opening is observed.

JIVO Oil · 12h shifts × 26 working days · 4 Sundays off
64%
of the September plan gets made under the baseline pattern

Run the floor as it runs today and September makes 27,65,370 L — ₹48.93 Cr of output — and ships 27,60,307 L, against a plan of 43,23,300 L across 84 SKUs. That is +30.5% on the 21,19,237 L the plant actually made in August. The missing 15,57,930 L is not idle will — it is storage, materials and the clock, plus 66,000 L that no configured line can make at all.

What the demand stream really is

real vs forecast — split by channel, never mixed

Said plainly: roughly 64% of the demand this plan serves is forecast, not orders. Of 2,029 demand rows across 26 order dates, 121 are real orders on the books and 1,908 are the monthly plan written as dated buckets — 64.3% of the stream by litres. Nobody has placed the forecast rows.

Real orders — 35.7% by litres. 121 rows (TRADE 120 · MART 1) · 12,88,754 pcs · ₹28.23 Cr
Forecast — 64.3% by litres FORECAST 1,908 rows · 18,01,779 pcs · ₹49.24 Cr
The forecast share moves with the unit: 64.3% by litres · 58.3% by pieces · 63.56% by value.
Kept separable by design: the demand stream MIXES real orders and the plan as dated FORECAST buckets — forecast rows are triple-tagged (channel=FORECAST, docnum FCST-*, customer '(forecast — not yet ordered)') and must stay visually distinct.
ASSUMED the ecom half of the plan has NO weekly dating in EXIM — it is spread evenly across working days as a DECLARED ASSUMPTION (FCST-W0 rows).

What binds the month

three walls, in the order the plan hits them

12 of the 13 blocked products wait on short oil — 29 of the 37 attempts, 20 of those on loose refined olive oil RM0000001 alone. Only 0 trace to a zero-stock packaging item; 3 wait on other packaging (2 of the 13 are short in two classes at once). ↓ the loop · → the order-by list

Extra hours turn into litres only until storage and materials push back — which is why the biggest pattern is not the best one. “Extra hours → litres” is the share of the additional line-hours each pattern actually converts. Two of the patterns front-load — long shifts early, a shorter tail after the switch day — to test whether the early gain survives a cheaper back half.

The front-load-then-taper question, answered by the same engine: taper to 12h after day 13 and the month keeps only 45.6% of the flat-22h gain; taper to 18h after day 13 and 84.1% of that gain survives on 80% of flat-22h's extra hours. Flat 24h remains max output; plain Sundays-on (12h × 30d) remains the best hours-to-litres conversion at 82.7%.
Sunday wages are not modelled in any of these patterns — “cheapest” is about hours converting to litres, not wage cost.
pct_extra_hours_used = (line-hours used beyond baseline) / (extra line-hours offered); offered = scenario available line-hours − baseline available line-hours, where available = shift ceiling × working days × number of lines, and a tapered pattern uses its per-phase ceilings (front through the switch day, tail after) derived from its own day files; every figure computed from the scenario artifacts.
every pattern shown has a full 30-day artifact on disk (summary, day files, events) — including the 18h-tail taper an earlier build flagged as missing.

The loop — how a shortage becomes a run

one chain from the plan’s event stream

The plan’s whole supply story is one loop, run 43 times: a blocker surfaces, the planner orders — usually the same day, sometimes days after the wall first bites — the measured lead time passes, the material lands, and the freed SKU runs where the calendar still allows. Not every chain gets all the way round (the tally below); the largest that closes end-to-end:

  1. 1Blocked
    1 Sep

    15 SKUs want LOOSE REFINED OLIVE OIL (RM0000001) and the store cannot feed them.

    →
  2. 2Ordered
    1 Sep

    The planner orders 3,71,512 L the same day. OIL

    →
  3. 3The wait
    11 days pass

    The measured oil lead time is 11 days — the sim assumes supply arrives exactly on it.

    →
  4. 4Lands
    12 Sep

    The material arrives and the blocker clears on 12 Sep — after 11 days of waiting.

    →
  5. 5Runs
    12 Sep

    First run out of the clear: ZANO EXTRA VIRGIN OLIVE1 LTR 16 PCS — 1,250 L.

Every order the plan raises follows that same loop — a shortage the plan never orders against simply stays short. 39 of 43 order-chains land and unblock inside September — 32 of those see the freed SKU run again before month-end, 7 clear too late in the schedule to run — and 4 land only after 30 Sep. Leads run 6–11 days (6 d packaging, 11 d oil — measured). Watch the chains land day by day on the day pages. SIMULATED

This is a forward plan, not a record. September 2026 has not happened; only the 1-September opening is observed. The factory has not run this way.
Measured: the 31-Aug stock and open POs, the open order backlog, BOMs, line speeds and clearance, realise, lead times. Assumed (declared, flagged in the data): forecast demand buckets for volume not yet ordered, the even ecom spread, supply exactly on lead time, the invoice→truck lag, the observed line-efficiency derate, the storage ceiling (open question Q2), standing stock uncounted at open. Phone numbers are masked — September has no approval to show them.
Every number traces to sim/sep-inputs.json via scripts/gen-data.py.
